audience: Software builders who want to turn an idea into useful, expressive behavior
brief: Give this pocket pet a job. Tell a playful MiniMax Code CLI example through its real timer-ready, held-paused and happy-completion states. Make the changing face the memory point, with authentic early branding and beat-led music, not a generic feature inventory.

facts.text: MiniMax describes Coding and Work modes for its coding harness.
The product page describes agents teaming up to tackle tasks.
The product description includes working with images, video and audio, and creating scripts and voiceovers.
In the documented MiniMax Code CLI example, the first request adds a Pomodoro timer to an existing browser pet.
The follow-up requests hold-to-pause behavior for that timer.
The same example adds a completion celebration, shown by the happy pet in the browser footage.
This is a CLI example using an existing starter and BYOK. The maintainer finished the visual design; the visibly labeled ten-second demo is not generation time.

notes: Owner rejected the previous film as boring. The generic role relay also failed independent review for circular copy and the tiny blank desktop UI. The new private direction uses the approved real pocket-pet case: ready timer, paused sleepy face, then a smiling celebration. These are three different stills decoded from the official edited demo, not live interaction footage in our film. Show them large enough to read in both landscape and portrait; a single cropped pet is naturally portrait-oriented. Use cta-endcard with the cleared logo as an opening title if helpful, then three concise ui-showcase shots with textSlot captions and finally the exact supplied CTA. Prefer the ready/paused/celebrate stills; the preserved empty desktop screenshot is not the story. Do not return to a Coding/Work/Media inventory or claim the pet is the MiniMax logo or physical hardware. Required readable on-screen credit once: "CLI example · Maintainer-finished visuals". Do not claim the visual design or starter was generated from scratch, or confuse the visible ten-second demo timer with coding time. No test-count, performance, cost or outcome guarantee. Use audible procedural funk at 100 BPM and deliberate beat landings; a short chime can mark the happy face. Suggested 30-fps schedule with cut transitions: branded opener 0–69; ready 69–177; paused 177–285; celebrate 285–381; CTA 381–450. Product landings are local 21, so the three real-state reveals land at global 90/198/306; final CTA local 15 lands at 396. Keep enough read time, warm-white type, deep navy and cobalt/cyan. Show the authentic cleared mark early and on the ending. Preserve Explore MiniMax Code and agent.minimax.io exactly. Use only the confirmed case facts needed for this short story; keep the original general facts intact, not mandatory on-screen text.
